title: AI coding spend reviews: costs, output and ROI
summary: Run a monthly AI coding spend review with Weave. Connect costs, merged output, quality and delivery, then record what to renew, expand or investigate.
body_markdown:
Weave connects AI spending with the engineering work it supports: complexity-weighted merged output, explained pull-request analysis, code quality, reviews and delivery. Use it for a monthly investment review that gives engineering and finance a concrete basis for deciding where the next AI dollar should go.


## TL;DR


- Review AI costs and merged output for the same team, repositories and period.
- Inspect the code behind the output, then review quality and delivery alongside it.
- Use Weave's original research for context and your team's evidence for the investment decision.


Bring this review to the monthly budget meeting and revisit it before a renewal, seat expansion or major model change. Leave with a decision and a written record someone else can inspect.


## Bring three useful benchmarks to the review


Weave's research shows why this decision deserves attention. Keep these three views separate when presenting them.


**Platform-wide growth:** the[Q3 2026 AI Impact Report](https://weaveos.com/research/q3-2026) covers **22,623 engineers** . Average monthly output per employee rose **87%** , from **70 units in June to 131 in September 2026** . Average AI spend per employee per month grew **2.5×** , from **$231 to $575** . These monthly averages include engineers with AI spend or merged output in each month.


**The same organizations over time:** the report's constant organization cohort recorded a **3.1×** increase in median output per employee from **Q3 2025 to Q3 2026** . Those organizations were active in all five quarters. This is a separate view of the same organizations progressing over time.


**Output per AI dollar:** the[Weave Index](https://weaveos.com/data/return-on-token-spend) reports **0.171411 estimated expert hours per attributed dollar** for **October 2026** , across **9,558 engineers** with both AI spend and merged output that month. This is the **November 3, 2026 snapshot** . The monthly spend/output-matched group can change.


Output uses Weave's complexity-weighted estimate of expert effort. Each benchmark has its own population, period and unit; bring those labels into the review with the number.


## Run the investment review in four steps


### 1. Name the decision and choose the scope


Write down the decision first: renew a coding tool, add seats, expand a successful workflow or investigate rising costs. Choose the team, connected repositories and review period, then choose a comparable baseline.


Keep the scope consistent. If the team added engineers or took on different work, record that context alongside the comparison. The review should explain the change well enough to support a budget decision.


### 2. Connect the spending to the team


[Token Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence) brings together AI usage, supported provider billing, tool telemetry and configured subscription costs. Review spending by engineer and team, with model detail where the source provides it.


Use the cost-source labels to see the basis of each amount. Reconcile seats, included allowances and usage charges with the bill, and record shared costs separately. This gives finance a clear account of what is being reviewed.


### 3. Inspect the work that merged


[Code Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/code-intelligence) analyzes the changes inside a pull request. Silk 1 considers intent, complexity, risk and dependencies across files, then explains its estimate of expert effort.


Open representative merged PRs from the review period. Read the explanation, inspect the diff and ask whether the output reflects the work your team intended to fund. This is a concrete advantage of reviewing complexity-weighted output alongside spending: the investment discussion has code-level evidence behind it.


### 4. Put quality and delivery beside output


[Engineering Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence) adds review activity, review cycles, reverts, code turnover and delivery measures. Check whether higher output reached production cleanly and whether review or rework became a bottleneck.


Use an appropriate post-merge observation window. Review the results with the people who own the work, then choose the next action. The[AI ROI methodology](https://weaveos.com/methodology/ai-roi) explains the measures and cost attribution behind this process.

## Buyer questions


### How do I decide whether a higher AI bill is justified?


Review what changed in merged output, quality and delivery for the same team and period. A higher bill can support more valuable work; use the underlying PRs and spending detail to explain the result.


### What should I check before adding more coding-tool seats?


Check current adoption, paid-seat activity, the workflows producing useful output and any review bottlenecks. Expand access with a named team, a budget and a follow-up review.


### Can I use the public Index as my team's target?


Use it as published context. Your decision should use your team's connected costs, repositories and work mix. The Index's estimated expert-hour ratio describes modeled output per attributed dollar, rather than recorded hours saved or a financial ROI percentage.
